note:
ROUND 4 of the explainer for /pages/firming-skin-density — templates/page.firming-skin-density.json, section `content`, block `causes`, 'What Causes Loss of Firmness?'.

MALCOLM, 2026-08-25: 'lets show the breakage of the skin in the middle - in between the left and the right side that are more healthy.'

ONE CHANGE ONLY: THE DAMAGE MOVES FROM THE RIGHT END TO THE MIDDLE. Rounds 1-3 ran the loss as a falloff from one end of the block to the other. Now the block is sound at BOTH ends and fails through the CENTRE. Everything else is held exactly where round 3 left it — the square-on front elevation, the block filling the frame, the transcribed layer stack, the skin palette, every negative.

WHY THIS IS BETTER, AND IT IS NOT ONLY COMPOSITION. A falloff running left to right has a direction, and a direction reads as a sequence — this end became that end, which is a before-and-after argument wearing a gradient. Loss framed by intact tissue on both sides has no arrow in it: it is a zone of the same skin that has lost its structure, which is what the copy actually describes. It also puts the subject in the middle of a square frame, which is where the eye lands and where the media box's own centre crop is safest.

THE ONE THING THAT WILL WRECK THIS ROUND IS SYMMETRY. Ask any of these engines for 'sound at both ends, damaged in the middle' and the obvious solution it reaches for is a mirrored diptych — the right half rendered as a flip of the left, with the damage on the seam. That is precisely the split-screen the whole family has negated since r3 of the copper-peptide set, and it would be worse here because it is disguised as one picture. So every slot now states that the two intact ends must NOT match: different fibre paths, different lobule sizes and spacing, different surface undulation, the damage zone off-centre rather than dead centre and wider on one side than the other. 'No mirror image, no mirrored halves, no symmetry, no reflection' are added to the negatives by name.

AND IT MUST BE A THINNING, NOT A HOLE. 'Breakage' here means the STRUCTURES breaking — fibres parting, granules crumbling, lobules collapsing — not the block being cut, punched or torn in two. A gap through the block reads as a wound, and a wound is a different and much worse claim than a loss of density. The block stays one continuous piece across its whole width; what happens in the middle is that the layers within it thin, part and sag. No hole, no crater, no cut, no severed block, no gap right through — all negated.

WHAT THE MIDDLE LOOKS LIKE, in every slot: the granular band loosens and crumbles into a drift of fine specks; the fibre bundles thin, lose their pearl lustre to a dull chalky greyed-beige, fray apart into loose splayed strands and part with the ends drawn back and curled; the lobules shrink into a run of much smaller beads and slump, leaving a soft hollow under the layers above; and the surface, unsupported, sinks into a long slack valley that is deepest over the worst of it. That last one is the payoff — it is the only part of the picture a shopper reads as their own face.

THREE SLOTS, ONE PICTURE, THREE SEVERITIES:
  A  compacted stack, a BROAD gentle zone of loss across the middle third — the faithful one, closest to r3 C nbp_flash_02 which was the round-3 leader
  B  compacted stack, a NARROWER and deeper zone with a distinct valley folded into the surface — more dramatic, and the one at most risk of reading as a seam, so it is offered rather than assumed
  C  the same broad zone with the strata FLOATING APART on air gaps, as in the luma_02 Malcolm chose in r2

STILL GENERATED REFERENCE-FREE, for the r3 reason: the change being asked for is compositional, and an attached reference locks the composition it already has. It also keeps FLUX.2 in the run.

CARRIED OVER UNCHANGED: square 2048x2048 (the row height in `media-with-text` is set by the master's own aspect, so anything else makes this block taller than its five siblings); the r3/matrixyl house register; the r2 skin palette and its ban on teal, clinical blue, copper and gold; no lettering, arrows or callout furniture; the family's delivery spheres, light shafts, peptide chains and starburst glints stay negated because this block is the damage and the next block on the page is the repair; no MMP drawn as a character.

JUDGE AT 100% AND AGAIN AT RENDER SIZE. Two checks, both learned on this brief: TEXTURE COHERENCE, because a wall of horizontal pearl bundles seen flat-on is one step from noodles or piped icing; and HOLLOW TUBE ENDS, which appeared on r3 A nbp_pro_01 and B nbp_flash_02 — parted fibres rendered as cut piping with an open bore, which reads as tubing rather than fibre. Solid parted ends only.

slots.title: A · compacted stack, a broad zone of loss across the middle, sound at both ends
slots.prompt:
Soft three-dimensional medical explainer illustration in the style of premium skincare advertising: smooth glossy CGI, luminous and dreamy, high-key on a pale hazy gradient background. Square format.

A block of skin is shown in cross-section SEEN SQUARE ON FROM THE FRONT. The camera is level with the middle of the block and directly in front of it, so the cut face is exactly parallel to the picture plane, its edges horizontal, with no perspective and no convergence. The top surface is not seen as a plane — at most the thinnest sliver of it shows along the upper edge. The block runs from the left edge of the frame to the right edge and fills nearly the whole height. The tissue is a soft desaturated peach-cream, warm, pale and matte; nothing in the frame is dyed or tinted.

THE LAYERS SIT DIRECTLY ON ONE ANOTHER, IN CONTACT, one solid continuous slab. From top to bottom, in this exact order: a narrow band of surface made of soft rounded raised pads in an irregular tile pattern, blush-peach and slightly felted; directly beneath it a thin smooth band of pale cream, finely laminated where it is cut; beneath that a thick band of small rounded pale-pink granules packed densely together like a fine foam of tiny cells; then a thin smooth peach plate; then, filling the middle of the block, a deep zone of long thick glossy fibre bundles in a pale pearl ivory, almost white with only the faintest warm gold in their highlights, lying in loose parallel horizontal waves through a soft peach-cream ground, glassy and translucent and crisply defined against it, separated by material and not by colour; then a second thin smooth peach plate; and at the bottom a deep cushion of large smooth glossy rounded lobules in a pearly cream-blush, packed in two rows like a bed of eggs. The whole block stands on a thin clear colourless glass plate.

THE BLOCK IS SOUND AT BOTH ENDS AND HAS FAILED THROUGH THE MIDDLE. At the left edge and again at the right edge the tissue is healthy: the granular band is dense and even, the fibre bundles are thick, numerous, brightly pearlescent and closely woven, the cushion of lobules is deep and full and round, and the surface above is level and taut.

Across the middle third the structure has broken down. The granules there loosen and crumble away into a drift of fine pale specks in the air. The fibre bundles thin and lose their lustre, the pearl going dull, chalky and greyed-beige and the glassy surface turning matte; they fray apart into loose splayed strands and several have parted outright, the two ends drawn back from each other and curled, blunt and solid where they end. The gaps between them widen until that part of the zone is mostly empty space. Beneath, the lobules shrink and flatten into a run of much smaller beads and slump downward, leaving a soft hollow under the layers above. And the surface, with nothing left to hold it up, sinks into a long slack valley that is deepest over the worst of the damage.

THE BLOCK REMAINS ONE CONTINUOUS PIECE ACROSS ITS WHOLE WIDTH. The middle is thinned, parted and sagging — it is never cut through, never punched open, and there is no gap from top to bottom.

THE TWO SOUND ENDS ARE NOT ALIKE. The fibre bundles take different paths on the left from the right, the lobules are of different sizes and spacing, and the surface undulates differently on each side. The damaged zone is not centred exactly: it sits a little off to one side and is wider on one flank than the other, and it fades into the healthy tissue through a slow smooth gradient with no line, no seam and no edge. Nothing in the picture is repeated, flipped or mirrored.

Nothing is arriving and nothing is being rebuilt. Soft diffuse light, no hard shadow, shallow depth of field. Glossy, luminous, immaculate.
